/-- Completing after left tensor placement agrees with left tensor placement
after completing the local submeasurement.

This is the bookkeeping needed to apply the standard completion-distance
identity on the product Hilbert space while returning the local completed
projective measurement appearing in the paper. -/
private lemma qSDD_leftPlaced_completeAtOutcome_eq
    {Outcome : Type*} {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ιA) (a0 : Outcome) :
    qSDD ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) A)
        (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) B) a0).toSubMeas =
      qSDD ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) A)
        (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB)
          (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas) := by
  have hcomplete_outcome :
      ∀ a : Outcome,
        (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome
            (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) B) a0).toSubMeas.outcome a =
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB)
            (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas).outcome a := by
    intro a
    by_cases h : a = a0
    · subst h
      ext i j
      rcases i with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
      rcases j with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
      by_cases h₁ : i₁ = j₁ <;> by_cases h₂ : i₂ = j₂ <;>
        simp [Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome, leftPlacedSubMeas, leftTensor,
          sub_eq_add_neg, h₁, h₂, add_comm, add_assoc]
    · ext i j
      rcases i with ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
      rcases j with ⟨j₁, j₂⟩
      by_cases h₁ : i₁ = j₁ <;> by_cases h₂ : i₂ = j₂ <;>
        simp [Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome, leftPlacedSubMeas, leftTensor, h, h₁, h₂]
  unfold qSDD qSDDCore
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro a _
  rw [hcomplete_outcome a]

/-- If the missing left total of a projective submeasurement is small on the
state, then the canonical completion is close to the submeasurement after left
tensor placement. -/
private lemma qSDD_completeAtOutcomeProj_leftPlaced_le_of_total_gap
    {Outcome : Type*} {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized)
    (P : ProjSubMeas Outcome ιA) (a0 : Outcome) {ζ : Error}
    (hgap : 1 - ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) P.toSubMeas.total) ≤ ζ) :
    qSDD ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas)
      (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB)
        (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcomeProj P a0).toSubMeas) ≤ ζ := by
  let R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB) :=
    (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB)) -
      (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas).total
  have hraw :
      qSDD ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas)
          (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome
            (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas) a0).toSubMeas ≤
        ζ := by
    have hcomp :
        qSDD ψ (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas)
            (Preliminaries.completeAtOutcome
              (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas) a0).toSubMeas =
          ev ψ (R * R) := by
      simpa [R] using
        (Preliminaries.completion_self_distance ψ
          (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas) a0)
    have hR_nonneg : 0 ≤ R := by
      dsimp [R]
      exact sub_nonneg.mpr (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas).total_le_one
    have hR_le_one : R ≤ 1 := by
      dsimp [R]
      exact sub_le_self (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ιA × ιB))
        (leftPlacedSubMeas (ιB := ιB) P.toSubMeas).total_nonneg
    have hR_sq_le : R * R ≤ R :=
      MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self hR_nonneg hR_le_one
    have hR_sq_ev : ev ψ (R * R) ≤ ev ψ R :=
      ev_mono ψ _ _ hR_sq_le
    have hR_ev : ev ψ R ≤ ζ := by
      have hR_eq :
          ev ψ R =
            1 - ev ψ (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) P.toSubMeas.total) := by
        dsimp [R]
        rw [ev_sub]
        simp [ev_one_of_isNormalized ψ hψ]
      rw [hR_eq]
      exact hgap
    rw [hcomp]
    exact le_trans hR_sq_ev hR_ev
  have hq_eq :=
    qSDD_leftPlaced_completeAtOutcome_eq ψ P.toSubMeas P.toSubMeas a0
  rw [hq_eq] at hraw
  simpa [Preliminaries.completeAtOutcomeProj_toSubMeas] using hraw

/-!
# Preliminary completion lemmas

Structural completion helpers that stay close to `completeAtOutcome` while
keeping only the light projectivity dependencies from
`SwitchSandwichPrep/Core.lean`.

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

/-- Completing a projective submeasurement at a distinguished outcome preserves
projectivity. The residual effect `1 - P.total` is a projection orthogonal to
`P.outcome a0`, so the completed effect remains idempotent. -/
noncomputable def completeAtOutcomeProj {Outcome : Type*}
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (P : ProjSubMeas Outcome ι) (a0 : Outcome) : ProjMeas Outcome ι := by
  classical
  refine
    { toMeasurement := completeAtOutcome P.toSubMeas a0
      proj := ?_ }
  intro a
  by_cases ha : a = a0
  · subst a
    let T : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := P.total
    let Pa : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := P.outcome a0
    let R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 1 - T
    have hTT : T * T = T := by
      simpa [T] using projSubMeas_total_proj P
    have hPaT : Pa * T = Pa := by
      simpa [Pa, T] using projSubMeas_outcome_mul_total_eq_outcome P a0
    have hPa_star : IsStarProjection Pa :=
      isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨by simpa [Pa] using P.proj a0,
        (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (P.outcome_pos a0)).isHermitian.eq⟩
    have hT_star : IsStarProjection T :=
      isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨hTT,
        (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp P.total_nonneg).isHermitian.eq⟩
    have hR_star : IsStarProjection R := by
      simpa [R] using hT_star.one_sub
    have hPaR : Pa * R = 0 := by
      calc
        Pa * R = Pa * (1 - T) := by rfl
        _ = Pa - Pa * T := by rw [mul_sub, mul_one]
        _ = 0 := by simp [hPaT]
    have hproj :
        (P.outcome a0 + (1 - P.total)) * (P.outcome a0 + (1 - P.total)) =
          P.outcome a0 + (1 - P.total) := by
      simpa [Pa, R] using (hPa_star.add hR_star hPaR).isIdempotentElem.eq
    simpa [completeAtOutcome] using hproj
  · simpa [completeAtOutcome, ha] using P.proj a

@[simp] theorem completeAtOutcomeProj_toMeasurement {Outcome : Type*}
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (P : ProjSubMeas Outcome ι) (a0 : Outcome) :
    (completeAtOutcomeProj P a0).toMeasurement = completeAtOutcome P.toSubMeas a0 :=
  rfl

/-- A paper-local projective submeasurement (each effect is idempotent).

There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: any such default would
again collapse to the degenerate zero family. -/
structure ProjSubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    extends SubMeas α ι where
  proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a

/-- A paper-local projective measurement (complete POVM + projective). -/
structure ProjMeas (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    extends Measurement α ι where
  proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a

/-- For a trivial distinguished-outcome projective measurement, every outcome operator
is idempotent. -/
private theorem ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_proj
    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a₀ a : α) :
    (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a *
        (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a =
      (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a := by
  classical
  by_cases h : a = a₀ <;> simp [Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome, h]

/-- ⚠️ DEGENERATE — Construct a trivial projective measurement where only the
distinguished outcome `a₀` is the identity and all other outcomes are zero.

This is a valid projective POVM but highly degenerate: see the discussion at
`Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome`.  Prefer calling this function
explicitly (with a chosen outcome) rather than relying on the ambient
`Inhabited` instance.  As for `Measurement`, there is intentionally no ambient
`Inhabited (ProjMeas α ι)` instance. -/
noncomputable def ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome
    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (a₀ : α) : ProjMeas α ι where
  toMeasurement := Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome a₀
  proj := ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_proj a₀

/-!
# Quantum states and tensor placement for the low individual degree test

Core quantum-state definitions together with tensor-placement operators.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- A PSD density matrix indexed by `ι`.

There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero matrix is PSD but
not a physical state of unit trace, so an ambient default would silently
trivialize later statements. Use `IsNormalized` to additionally require
`τ(ρ) = 1`.

This remains the ambient state space for the current LDT development: strategy
packages in `LDT/Test/StrategyCore.lean`, the SWAP-symmetry API `PermInvState`,
and the expectation-value lemmas in `LDT/Basic/OperatorExpectations.lean` are all
stated for arbitrary density matrices, not only pure states. -/
structure QuantumState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
  density : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
  density_psd : 0 ≤ density := by positivity

/-- Unit normalized trace for the concrete matrix carried by a state. -/
def QuantumState.IsNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) : Prop :=
  MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1

/-- A normalized state has a nonempty carrier: if the carrier were empty, the
trace would vanish and `normalizedTrace = 0 / 0 = 0`, contradicting `= 1`. -/
theorem QuantumState.IsNormalized.nonempty {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {ψ : QuantumState ι} (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized) : Nonempty ι := by
  by_contra h
  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
  letI := h
  rw [QuantumState.IsNormalized] at hψ
  have hzero : MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 0 := by
    simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
  exact zero_ne_one (hzero.symm.trans hψ)

/-- The scaled rank-one density matrix attached to a state vector.

Because this development uses the normalized trace `τ(A) = tr(A) / dim`, the
quantum state represented by a unit vector `ψ` is `dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|` rather than the
raw projector `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|`. This scaling makes `τ(ρ) = 1` and keeps `ev` aligned
with the paper's bra-ket expectations. -/
noncomputable def pureDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : ι → ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
  (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • Matrix.vecMulVec ψ (star ψ)

/-- Swap the two tensor coordinates of a bipartite state vector. -/
def swapVector {ι : Type*} (ψ : ι × ι → ℂ) : ι × ι → ℂ :=
  fun ij => ψ (ij.2, ij.1)

/-- A pure-state witness as a unit vector in the ambient finite Hilbert space.

The associated density matrix is `pureDensity ψ.vector = dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|`, so that
coercing to `QuantumState` preserves the paper's scalar `⟨ψ|X|ψ⟩` formulas
despite our use of the normalized trace. -/
structure PureState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] where
  vector : ι → ℂ
  unit : star vector ⬝ᵥ vector = 1

namespace PureState

/-- The coordinate-basis vector has unit self-dot product. -/
private theorem basis_unit {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (i : ι) :
    star (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ⬝ᵥ
        (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = 1 := by
  rw [dotProduct]
  simp

/-- The coordinate-basis pure state at a distinguished basis vector. -/
noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (i : ι) : PureState ι where
  vector := fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0
  unit := basis_unit i

/-- The density matrix represented by a pure-state witness. -/
noncomputable def density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
  pureDensity ψ.vector

theorem density_psd {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    0 ≤ ψ.density := by
  refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
  exact (Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star ψ.vector).smul
    (by positivity : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℂ))

noncomputable def toQuantumState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) : QuantumState ι where
  density := ψ.density
  density_psd := ψ.density_psd

noncomputable instance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] :
    Coe (PureState ι) (QuantumState ι) where
  coe := toQuantumState

@[simp] theorem coe_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    (ψ : QuantumState ι).density = ψ.density := rfl

theorem normalizedTrace_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1 := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
  unfold density pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
  rw [Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec, dotProduct_comm, ψ.unit]
  change ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) * 1) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) = 1
  rw [mul_one, div_self hcard]

theorem toQuantumState_isNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    (ψ : QuantumState ι).IsNormalized := by
  simpa [QuantumState.IsNormalized] using ψ.normalizedTrace_density

theorem normalizedTrace_density_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (ψ : PureState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X) =
      star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
  calc
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X)
      = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * (ψ : QuantumState ι).density) := by
          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * ψ.density) := by rfl
    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
          ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector))) := by
          simp [density, pureDensity]
    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
          MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)) := by
          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
          (((X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
          simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
          (((Matrix.vecMulVec (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
          rw [Matrix.mul_vecMulVec]
    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
          (((X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
          rw [Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
    _ = (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector := by
          field_simp [hcard]
    _ = star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
          rw [dotProduct_comm]

/-- Vector-level SWAP invariance for a bipartite pure-state witness.

This is stronger than density-level SWAP invariance: it records the paper's
honest vector symmetry and rules out antisymmetric vectors, even though those
vectors define SWAP-invariant density matrices. -/
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.CauchySchwarz


/-!
# Triangle Inequalities for State-Dependent Distance: Core

This module contains the main triangle-substitution estimates for approximate
measurements.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Symmetry of the question-level state-dependent distance. -/
lemma qSDD_symm
    {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
    qSDD ψ A B = qSDD ψ B A := by
  let F : Outcome → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := fun a => A.outcome a - B.outcome a
  let G : Outcome → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := fun a => B.outcome a - A.outcome a
  have hFG : F = fun a => -G a := by
    funext a
    dsimp [F, G]
    abel
  unfold qSDD qSDDCore
  change ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ ((F a)ᴴ * F a) = ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ ((G a)ᴴ * G a)
  rw [hFG]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
  intro a _
  change
    ev ψ ((-G a)ᴴ * (-G a)) = ev ψ ((G a)ᴴ * G a)
  simp

/-- Symmetry of the state-dependent distance relation. -/
lemma sddRel_symm
    {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) (δ : Error) :
    SDDRel ψ 𝒟 A B δ →
      SDDRel ψ 𝒟 B A δ := by
  intro ⟨h⟩
  constructor
  simpa [sddError, qSDD_symm] using h

/-- `prop:triangle-inequality-for-vectors-squared`.

For a finite family of operators `Dᵢ`, the squared norm of the summed vector
`(∑ᵢ Dᵢ) ψ` is controlled by the cardinality times the sum of the squared norms
of the individual vectors `Dᵢ ψ`. -/
theorem triangleInequalityForVectorsSquared
    {κ ι : Type*} [Fintype κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (D : κ → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    ev ψ ((∑ i, D i)ᴴ * (∑ i, D i)) ≤
      (Fintype.card κ : Error) * ∑ i, ev ψ ((D i)ᴴ * D i) := by
  simpa using ev_sum_conjTranspose_mul_sum_le ψ D

/-- The expectation of the difference of two submeasurement totals is controlled
by the state-dependent distance between the two outcome families, with the
finite-outcome Cauchy--Schwarz loss.

This is the total-operator analogue of the matching-mass estimates used in
`triangleSub`.  It is useful precisely when the right-register families are
submeasurements rather than measurements, so that their total operators need
not be the identity. -/
theorem subMeas_total_ev_gap_abs_le_sqrt_card_qSDD
    {Outcome ι : Type*} [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized)
    (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
    |ev ψ A.total - ev ψ B.total| ≤
      Real.sqrt (Fintype.card Outcome : Error) * Real.sqrt (qSDD ψ A B) := by
  let D : Outcome → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := fun a => A.outcome a - B.outcome a
  have htotal : A.total - B.total = ∑ a : Outcome, D a := by
    calc
      A.total - B.total
          = (∑ a : Outcome, A.outcome a) - ∑ a : Outcome, B.outcome a := by
              rw [← A.sum_eq_total, ← B.sum_eq_total]
      _ = ∑ a : Outcome, D a := by
              rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  have hev :
      ev ψ A.total - ev ψ B.total = ev ψ (∑ a : Outcome, D a) := by
    rw [← ev_sub, htotal]
  have hcs :
      |ev ψ (∑ a : Outcome, D a)| ≤
        Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) *
            (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)ᴴ)) *
          Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a))) := by
    simpa using ev_abs_mul_le_sqrt ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)
      (∑ a : Outcome, D a)
  have htri :
      ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a)) ≤
        (Fintype.card Outcome : Error) * qSDD ψ A B := by
    simpa [D, qSDD, qSDDCore] using triangleInequalityForVectorsSquared ψ D
  have hcard_nonneg : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card Outcome : Error) := by positivity
  have hsqrt_tri :
      Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a))) ≤
        Real.sqrt ((Fintype.card Outcome : Error) * qSDD ψ A B) :=
    Real.sqrt_le_sqrt htri
  calc
    |ev ψ A.total - ev ψ B.total|
        = |ev ψ (∑ a : Outcome, D a)| := by rw [hev]
    _ ≤ Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) *
          (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)ᴴ)) *
        Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a))) := hcs
    _ = Real.sqrt (ev ψ (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)) *
        Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a))) := by
          simp
    _ = Real.sqrt (ev ψ ((∑ a : Outcome, D a)ᴴ * (∑ a : Outcome, D a))) := by
          simp [ev_one_of_isNormalized ψ hψ]
    _ ≤ Real.sqrt ((Fintype.card Outcome : Error) * qSDD ψ A B) := hsqrt_tri
    _ = Real.sqrt (Fintype.card Outcome : Error) * Real.sqrt (qSDD ψ A B) := by
          rw [Real.sqrt_mul hcard_nonneg]

/-! ### Elementary max bound -/

/-- Adding `y` inside `max 0` changes the value by at most `|y|`. -/
lemma max_zero_add_le (x y : Error) :
    max 0 (x + y) ≤ max 0 x + |y| := by
  by_cases hxy : x + y < 0
  · rw [max_eq_left_of_lt hxy]
    positivity

/-!
# Preliminary comparison theorems: bipartite self-consistency (completion)

Completion-transfer lemmas for bipartite self-consistency.  The constant
`Unit`-family reductions identify `sddError` and `sscError` with their pointwise
forms, and the later lemmas compare a submeasurement with its completion.

## References

- `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex`
- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch03_preliminaries.tex`
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- For a constant `Unit`-indexed family, `sddError` reduces to `qSDD`. -/
lemma constFamily_sdd_unit
    {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
    sddError ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (constSubMeasFamily A) (constSubMeasFamily B) =
      qSDD ψ A B := by
  simp [sddError, avgOver, uniformDistribution, constSubMeasFamily]

/-- For a constant `Unit`-indexed family, `sscError` reduces to `qSSCDefect`. -/
lemma constFamily_ssc_unit
    {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A : SubMeas Outcome ι) :
    sscError ψ (uniformDistribution Unit) (constSubMeasFamily A) =
      qSSCDefect ψ A := by
  simp [sscError, avgOver, uniformDistribution, constSubMeasFamily]

/-- Completing `B` at `a0` changes only the missing mass, so the self-distance is
exactly the squared residual mass. -/
lemma completion_self_distance
    {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (B : SubMeas Outcome ι) (a0 : Outcome) :
    qSDD ψ B (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas =
      ev ψ (((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) - B.total) *
        ((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) - B.total)) := by
  classical
  let R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 1 - B.total
  have hsum :
      ∑ a : Outcome,
          ev ψ
            ((B.outcome a -
                (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas.outcome a)ᴴ *
              (B.outcome a -
                (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas.outcome a)) =
        ev ψ (R * R) := by
    have hBtotal_herm : B.totalᴴ = B.total := by
      exact (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp B.total_nonneg).isHermitian.eq
    have hsingle :
        ∑ a : Outcome,
          (if a = a0 then ev ψ (R * R) else 0) =
          ev ψ (R * R) := by
      simp
    calc
      ∑ a : Outcome,
          ev ψ
            ((B.outcome a -
                (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas.outcome a)ᴴ *
              (B.outcome a -
                (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas.outcome a))
        = ∑ a : Outcome, if a = a0 then ev ψ (R * R) else 0 := by
            refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
            intro a _
            by_cases ha : a = a0
            · subst ha
              have hRflip :
                  (B.total - 1) * (B.total - 1) =
                    (1 - B.total) * (1 - B.total) := by
                noncomm_ring
              simp [completeAtOutcome, R, hBtotal_herm, hRflip]
            · simp [completeAtOutcome, ha, ev_zero]
      _ = ev ψ (R * R) := hsingle
  simpa [qSDD, qSDDCore, R] using hsum

/-- Evaluating a completed polynomial submeasurement at a point is the same as
completing the evaluated submeasurement at the induced outcome. -/
lemma evaluateAt_completeAtOutcome
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (params : Parameters)
    [FieldModel params.q]
    (H : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι)
    (h0 : Polynomial params)
    (u : Point params) :
    evaluateAt params u (completeAtOutcome H h0).toSubMeas =
      (completeAtOutcome (evaluateAt params u H) (h0 u)).toSubMeas := by
  classical
  let R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 1 - H.total
  let L := evaluateAt params u (completeAtOutcome H h0).toSubMeas
  let Rhs := (completeAtOutcome (evaluateAt params u H) (h0 u)).toSubMeas
  have houtcome : L.outcome = Rhs.outcome := by
    funext b
    let S : Finset (Polynomial params) :=
      Finset.univ.filter fun h : Polynomial params => h u = b
    have hsplit :
        (∑ h ∈ S,
            if hh : h = h0 then H.outcome h + R else H.outcome h) =
          (∑ h ∈ S, H.outcome h) +
            ∑ h ∈ S, if h = h0 then R else 0 := by
      calc
        (∑ h ∈ S, if hh : h = h0 then H.outcome h + R else H.outcome h)
          = ∑ h ∈ S, (H.outcome h + if h = h0 then R else 0) := by
              refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Local (single-register) version of the completion bound.
This is the original proof, preserved verbatim so it can be called
by the bipartite wrapper below. -/
private lemma closenessAfterCompletion_core_local {Outcome : Type*}
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype Outcome]
    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
    (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized)
    (A : Measurement Outcome ι) (B : SubMeas Outcome ι)
    (a0 : Outcome) (δ ζ : Error) :
    SSCRel ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
        (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas) ζ →
    SDDRel ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
        (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas)
        (constSubMeasFamily B) δ →
    SDDRel ψ (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas)
      (constSubMeasFamily (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas)
      (2 * δ + 4 * Real.sqrt δ + 2 * ζ) := by
  intro ⟨hζ⟩ hdist
  rcases hdist with ⟨hδ⟩
  have hζ' :
      qSSCDefect ψ A.toSubMeas ≤ ζ := by
    simpa [constFamily_ssc_unit] using hζ
  have hδ' :
      qSDD ψ A.toSubMeas B ≤ δ := by
    simpa [constFamily_sdd_unit] using hδ
  have hBC :
      qSDD ψ B (completeAtOutcome B a0).toSubMeas =
        ev ψ (((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) - B.total) *
          ((1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) - B.total)) :=
    completion_self_distance ψ B a0
  let diagA : Error :=
    ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.toSubMeas.outcome a * A.toSubMeas.outcome a)
  let diagB : Error :=
    ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (B.outcome a * B.outcome a)
  let overlap : Error :=
    ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.toSubMeas.outcome a * B.outcome a)
  have hgap :
      |diagA - overlap| ≤ Real.sqrt δ ∧
        |overlap - diagB| ≤ Real.sqrt δ := by
    simpa [diagA, diagB, overlap, constSubMeasFamily, avgOver, uniformDistribution] using
      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.easyApproxFromApproxDelta_twoFamily ψ
        (uniformDistribution Unit) hψ
        (uniformDistribution_weight_sum_le_one Unit)
        (constSubMeasFamily A.toSubMeas)
        (constSubMeasFamily B) δ (by exact ⟨hδ⟩)
  have hgapA_raw :
      |diagA - overlap| ≤ Real.sqrt δ := hgap.1
  have hgapA :
      diagA - overlap ≤ Real.sqrt δ := by
    exact (abs_le.mp hgapA_raw).2
  have hgapB_raw :
      |overlap - diagB| ≤ Real.sqrt δ := hgap.2
  have hgapB :
      overlap - diagB ≤ Real.sqrt δ := by
    exact (abs_le.mp hgapB_raw).2
  have hdiagA_lb : 1 - ζ ≤ diagA := by
    have hssc :
        max 0
            (ev ψ A.toSubMeas.total -
              ∑ a : Outcome, ev ψ (A.toSubMeas.outcome a * A.toSubMeas.outcome a))
          ≤ ζ := by
      simpa [qSSCDefect, diagA] using hζ'
    have hinner :
        ev ψ A.toSubMeas.total - diagA ≤ ζ := by
      exact le_trans (le_max_right 0 (ev ψ A.toSubMeas.total - diagA)) hssc
    have hmassA : ev ψ A.toSubMeas.total = 1 := by
      simpa [A.total_eq_one] using ev_one_of_isNormalized ψ hψ
    linarith
  have hdiagB_lb : 1 - ζ - 2 * Real.sqrt δ ≤ diagB := by
    linarith
  have hresidual_le :

Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,\n`DESIGN.md` wins.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. The load-bearing citations:\n\n| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *\"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere.\"* |\n| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *\"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library.\"* |\n| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *\"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget.\"* |\n| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *\"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache.\"* |\n| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *\"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile.\"* |\n| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |\n| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *\"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround\"* |\n| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |\n| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *\"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade\"* |\n| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally the same holds:\n**every worktree runs its own `lake exe cache get`.**\n\n> **Tier 2 is never symlinked into a worktree.** A shared `.lake/packages` looks\n> attractive (it saves the download), but it is read-only only by convention, and\n> a single consumer running `lake update` mutates the tree for every other\n> worktree simultaneously. The download is cheap; a corrupted shared dependency\n> tree during a multi-agent session is not. `warm-worktree.sh` therefore fetches\n> per worktree, and `worktree-setup.sh` refuses to run `lake update` at all.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nAll runtime state lives under `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`, default\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`. Nothing in this tree is ever committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_4","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,260p' docs/anti_patterns.md\"","aggregated_output":"# Lean Proof-Evasion Anti-Patterns\n\nCatalog of subtle proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks\n(`sorry`-free, no forbidden tactics, all axioms standard) yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The active\ntrack here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\\*=RE\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nEvery GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local\nequivalent that *executes* here. Since 2026-09-01 the issue, PR, evidence and\nmerge **records** live on GitHub again (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`,\n`protocols/issues-prs.md`); what runs is still local. `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |\n| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |\n| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |\n| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |\n| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |\n| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |\n| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; (GitHub's\n   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)\n2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the\n   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the\n   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green\n   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix\n   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final\n   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.\n3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,\n   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix\n   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.\n4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and\n   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;\n   unset means enabled.\n5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`\n   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.\n6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies\n   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,\n   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.\n7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);\n   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.\n8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently\n   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a\n   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.\n9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid\n   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).\n10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README\n    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked\n    command.\n11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization\n    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT\n    exactly as to LDT.\n\n## Naming and identity conventions\n\n- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry\n  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy\n  (`issues-prs.md`). Dispatched\n  only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,\n  captures the `--json` event stream to\n  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to\n  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line\n  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.\n\n## Telemetry (research-paper data)\n\nAll appends are one-line JSON; schemas documented in `protocols/meta.md`.\n\n- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,\n  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,\n  output, reasoning), exit status, dispatcher.\n- `results/telemetry/stages.jsonl` — one line per project stage/substage\n  transition with timestamps and manual token/agent tallies.\n- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` — one line per full build / cache event:\n  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.\n- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,\n  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.\n- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an\n  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is\n  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.\n\n## Model policy\n\n- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/\n  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`).\n- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier; Fable-tier is\n  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial\n  verification).\n- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never\n  reviews its own diff.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

We do this first for the points.\nRecall that $\\mH_\\alice$ and $\\mH_\\bob$ denote the Hilbert spaces corresponding to\nregisters $\\alice$ and $\\bob$, respectively.\n\n\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:qld-4-10}\nThere exists a function $\\delta_Q(\\eps) = \\poly(\\eps)$ such that the following holds. \n\tFor every $x,z \\in \\F_q^m$ and $\\mH \\in \\{ \\mH_\\alice, \\mH_\\bob\\}$ there are projective measurements $\\{ \\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \\}_{a,b \\in \\F_q}$ acting on $\\mathcal{H} \\otimes (\\C^q)^{\\otimes \\nqubits}$ such that:\n\t\\begin{enumerate}\n\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \\in \\F_q^m$,\n\t\t\\begin{equation}\n\t\t\t\\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}\n\t\t\t(\\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\\alice \\alice'}  \\approx_{\\delta_Q} (\\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\\bob \\alice''}\\,.\n\t\t\\end{equation}\n\t\t\n\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Consistency with $\\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \\in \\F_q^m$,\n\t\t\\begin{gather}\n\t\t\t\\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}\n\t\t\t\t(\\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\\alice \\alice'} \\approx_{\\delta_Q} (\\hat{M}^{(\\Point,X),x}_{a} \\hat{M}^{(\\Point,Z),z}_b)_{\\bob \\alice''}\\;, \\\\\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}\n\t\t\t\t(\\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\\alice \\alice'} \\approx_{\\delta_Q} (\\hat{M}^{(\\Point,Z),z}_b  \\hat{M}^{(\\Point,X),x}_{a} )_{\\bob \\alice''}\\;.\n\t\t\\end{gather}\n              \\end{enumerate}\n                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations\n      also hold.\n\\end{lemma}\n\nThe construction of the measurements $\\{ \\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \\}$ whose existence is guaranteed in the lemma proceeds in three steps. In the first step, for every $(r,s)\\in\\F_q^2$ we combine the binary-outcome measurements $\\hat{M}^{(\\Point,X),x,r}_a$ and $\\hat{M}^{(\\Point,X),z,s}_b$; this is made possible by their approximate commutation as shown in Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}. Suppose that on average over $u, u'$ chosen uniformly from $\\F_2^t$, we have the following ``approximate linearity'' holds:\n\t\t\\[\n(\\mathcal{O}^u \\mathcal{O}^{u'})_{\\alice} \\approx_\\delta (\\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})_{\\alice}\n\t\t\\]\n\t\twhere the $\\approx$ statement is taken with respect to the state $\\ket{\\psi}$. \nThen there exists an extended state $\\ket{\\psi'}_{\\alice \\alice' \\bob} = \\ket{\\psi}_{\\alice \\bob} \\otimes \\ket{0}_{\\alice'}$ in an extended space $\\mathcal{H}_{\\alice} \\otimes \\mathcal{H}_\\bob \\otimes \\mathcal{H}_{\\alice'}$ and observables $\\{ \\mathcal{L}^u \\}$ acting on $\\mathcal{H}_\\alice \\otimes \\mathcal{H}_{\\alice'}$ such that for all $u, u' \\in \\F_2^t$, \n\t\t\\[\n\t\t\t\\mathcal{L}^u \\mathcal{L}^{u'} = \\mathcal{L}^{u + u'} \\qquad \\text{and} \\qquad (\\mathcal{L}^u)_{\\alice \\alice'} \\approx_\\delta (\\mathcal{O}^u)_\\alice \\,.\n\t\t\\]\n\t\tFurthermore, the observable $\\mathcal{L}^u = \\Id$ when $u = 0$.\n\t\\end{theorem}\n\t\t\n\t\tWe now give the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.\n\t\t\n\\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-10}]\nFor convenience in the proof we slightly abuse the notation $\\approx_\\delta$ to mean $\\approx_{\\poly(\\eps)}$ for some polynomial function $\\delta=\\poly(\\eps)$ that may differ each time the notation is used. \n\n\\textbf{First step: construction of projective binary measurements $\\{ \\hat{R}^\\omega_{a,b} \\}$.}\n\tFor every $\\omega = (x,z,r,s)$ and $a,b \\in \\F_2$, define a measurement operator\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\hat{R}^\\omega_{a,b} = \\hat{M}^{(\\Point,\\zpt),z,s}_{b} \\cdot \\hat{M}^{(\\Point,\\xpt),x,r}_{a} \\cdot \\hat{M}^{(\\Point,\\zpt),z,s}_{b} \\,.\n\t\\]\n\tIt is clear that $\\{ \\hat{R}^\\omega_{a,b} \\}_{a,b\\in\\F_2}$ is a POVM. This is\nthe axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).\n-/\ndef IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=\n  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i\n\n/--\nThe diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may\nvanish. It projects onto\nthe coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,\nso the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`; paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}\n    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=\n  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))\n\n/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the\ncanonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/\n/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`. Pure\nstates are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix\n`Measurement` structure.\n\n## References\n\nThe source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,\n`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.\nThe paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.\n-/\n\nopen scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder\n\nnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n\nopen MIPStarRE.LDT\nopen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n\n/--\nA finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question\npairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.\n-/\nstructure Game where\n  QuestionA : Type\n  QuestionB : Type\n  AnswerA : Type\n  AnswerB : Type\n  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]\n  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]\n  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]\n  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]\n  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]\n  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]\n  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]\n  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]\n  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)\n  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability\n  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool\n\nattribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype\n  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq\n  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq\n\n/--\nThe marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This\nis the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation\nis the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}\n    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\n    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=\n  M.postprocess Prod.fst\n\n/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in\n`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,\npaper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}\n    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\n    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=\n  M.postprocess Prod.snd\n\n/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/\ndef Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\n    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=\n  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)\n\n/--\nThe tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).\n-/\nstructure Strategy (G : Game) where\n  ιA : Type\n  ιB : Type\n  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]\n  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]\n  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]\n  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]\n  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)\n  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1\n  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA\n  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB\n\nattribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype\n  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq\n\n/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is\nthe finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.\n-/\ndef heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=\n  Matrix.kronecker A B\n\n/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance\nfunctionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally\nusing the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/\n/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space\naction underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/\nnoncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=\n  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ\n\n/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for\n`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/\nprivate noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)\n    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=\n  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=\n    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)\n  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ\n  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re\n\n/--\nThe tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born\nprobabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=\n  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>\n    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,\n      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)\n\n/--\nThe tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite\nstrategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested\nfor `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is\nintentionally not asserted here.\n-/\nnoncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=\n  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))\n\nend MIPStarRE.QPBT\nimport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs\n\n/-!\n# Quantitative state and operator distances\n\nThe blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the\ncorresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant\nestimates to later proof stages.\n\n## References\n\nThese are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.\n-/\n\nopen scoped BigOperators\n\nnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n\nopen MIPStarRE.LDT\nopen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n\n/--\nSquared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`\n(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]\n    [DecidableEq ι]\n    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=\n  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2\n\n/--\nAverage squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This\nis `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,\nwith paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}\n    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)\n    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=\n  avgOver μ (fun x =>\n    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)\n\nend MIPStarRE.QPBT\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
