{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_24","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,360p' MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinear.lean && sed -n '1,280p' MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean\"","aggregated_output":"import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionUniform\n\n/-!\n# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions\n\nThe question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite\ngraph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear\nmap to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure\nneeded by later formalization stages.\n\n## References\n\nThe source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and\n`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.\nThe paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`\nand `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.\n-/\n\nopen scoped BigOperators\n\nnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n\nopen MIPStarRE.LDT\n\nvariable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n\n/--\nThe source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive\npredicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is\nrejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same\npublic predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together\nwith its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation\ndeviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes\n`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,\npaper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ninductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]\n    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where\n  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0\n  | succ {ell : ℕ}\n      (S₁ : Finset ι)\n      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))\n      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)\n      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :\n      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)\n\n/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary\ncoordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,\nblueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ndef coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=\n  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0\n\n/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for\n`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ndef CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n    {K : Type*} [Field K] :\n    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)\n  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0\n  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>\n      fun x =>\n        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x\n        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x\n\n/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a\nLean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ndef CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]\n    {K : Type*} [Field K] :\n    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop\n  | _, .zero, _ => True\n  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>\n      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \\ S₁)\n\n/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree\nencoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ndef IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]\n    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)\n    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=\n  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,\n    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L\n\n/--\n`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint\n`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.\n-/\ndef IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=\n  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L\n\n/--\nThe distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common\nuniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]\n    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :\n    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=\n  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))\n\n/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left\ncoordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member\n`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate\ninfrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.\n-/\ndef condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]\n    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))\n    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))\n    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=\n  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)\n  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)\n  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)\n\n/--\nConcatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is\n`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, with\npaper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.\nThe direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the\nlevel proof remains deferred in this skeleton.\n-/\ntheorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]\n    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}\n    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}\n    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}\n    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)\n    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →\n      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :\n    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)\n      (condLinearConcat L R) := by\n  sorry\n\n/--\nThe graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge\n`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of\n`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;\npaper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.\nThe underlying graph-distribution definition is\n`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]\n    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=\n  Distribution.uniformOnFinset\n    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)\n\n/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/\ntheorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]\n    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :\n    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by\n  sorry\n\nend MIPStarRE.QPBT\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.Polynomials\n\n/-!\n# The low-degree encoding\n\nThis module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials\nand packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.\n\n## References\n\nThe source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,\n`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\nThe polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from\n`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).\n-/\n\nopen scoped BigOperators\nopen MvPolynomial\n\nnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n\n/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/\n/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index\ntype in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\n-/\nabbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool\n\n/--\nThe representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and\nzero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in\n`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).\n-/\nnoncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :\n    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=\n  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)\n\n/--\nThe multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial\nrepresentatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by\nfunctional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}\n    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=\n  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y\n\n/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in\n`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/\n/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint\n`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}\n    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=\n  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)\n\n/--\nThe indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.\nBlueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\n-/\nnoncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}\n    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=\n  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)\n\n/--\nThe defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to\nEquation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `lem:indicator-vector` in the\nblueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin\n`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.\nIt is a proof obligation in stage 4.1.\n-/\ntheorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}\n    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :\n    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by\n  sorry\n\nend MIPStarRE.QPBT\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

## Submeasurements and measurements -/\n\n/--\nA submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices\n`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.\n-/\nstructure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where\n  /-- The effect operators. -/\n  effect : α → Op d\n  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/\n  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a\n  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/\n  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1\n\n/--\nA measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.\n-/\nstructure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\n    extends Submeasurement α d where\n  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/\n  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1\n\n/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/\n\nnamespace Submeasurement\n\nvariable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\nvariable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]\n\n/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/\n\n/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/\nnoncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=\n  ∑ a, M.effect a\n\n/--\nData processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over\nfibers.\n-/\nnoncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where\n  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a\n  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a\n  sum_le_one := by\n    calc\n      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a\n          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect\n      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one\n\n/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/\ntheorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :\n    M.total ≤ 1 := by\n  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one\n\n/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/\ntheorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :\n    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=\n  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm\n\n/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/\ntheorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :\n    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by\n  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm\n\nend Submeasurement\n\nnamespace Measurement\n\nvariable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\nvariable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]\n\n/--\nBuild a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.\n\nThis constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives\nthe inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper\nsites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.\n-/\ndef ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)\n    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where\n  effect := effect\n  pos := pos\n  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one\n  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one\n\n/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/\ntheorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :\n    M.total = 1 :=\n  M.sum_eq_one\n\n/--\nPostprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.\n\nThis formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping\nthe effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM\nremains a POVM after postprocessing.\n-/\nnoncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where\n  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f\n  sum_eq_one := by\n    calc\n      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a\n          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect\n      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one\n\n@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :\n    (M.postprocess f).effect b =\n      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=\n  rfl\n\n@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]\n    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :\n    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=\n  rfl\n\nend Measurement\n\n/-! ## Overlap definitions -/\n\nsection Overlap\n\nvariable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]\nvariable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]\n\n/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/\nnoncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=\n  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)\n\n/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/\nnoncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=\n  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)\n\nend Overlap\n\nend MIPStarRE.Quantum\nimport MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic\nimport MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order\nimport MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.TracePairing\nimport MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.BlockDiagonal\nimport MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace\n\n/-!\n# Finite-dimensional matrix layer for the MIP*=RE project\n\nThis aggregate module preserves the historical `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`\nimport path while the underlying facts are organized into mathematical leaves:\nbasic operator and trace facts, positive-semidefinite order and cone facts,\nreal trace-pairing representation, block-diagonal order facts, and normalized\ntrace/projector material.\n\n## References\n\nThe declarations re-exported here collect the finite-dimensional matrix and PSD\nfacts from Mathlib for the project's quantum layer and the LDT development\nformalizing `references/ldt-paper/`.\n-/\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_27","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '17,105p' blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex\"","aggregated_output":"\\begin{definition}[The classical low individual degree game: parameters and registers]\\label{def:ld-game}\n\t\\uses{def:game, def:admissible-size}\n\t% The source fixes \\N to be the set of positive integers\n\t% (references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:6) and takes m, d, ldc in \\N\n\t% (references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:33-35),\n\t% so the positivity below is the source's implicit domain, stated explicitly.\n\t% It is load-bearing: at d = 0 or k = 0 the prefactor a(dmk)^a of delta_ld in\n\t% lem:ld-soundness vanishes, and at d = 0 the resulting exact conclusions fail\n\t% (e.g. at (q,m,d,k) = (2,1,0,1) with eps = 1). The case k = 0, though it would\n\t% hold trivially, is likewise outside the source's domain and is omitted.\n\tThe game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is parametrized by a tuple $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$, where $m, d, k \\ge 1$ are integers, $q \\in \\N$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\\ref{def:admissible-size}), and $m$ divides $q$. We write $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ to emphasize the dependence on the parameter tuple. The type set of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} = \\{\\mathsf{Point}, \\mathsf{ALine}, \\mathsf{DLine}\\}\\;,\n\t\\]\n\tand the distribution over type pairs $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ is uniform over $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$. The ambient space is the direct sum $V = V_X \\oplus V_I \\oplus V_V$ of three register subspaces: the \\emph{point register} $V_X \\cong \\F_q^m$, the \\emph{coordinate register} $V_I \\cong \\F_q$, and the \\emph{direction register} $V_V \\cong \\F_q^m$. Elements of $V$ are identified with triples $(u,s,v) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q \\times \\F_q^m$. The question distribution and the win predicate of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ are specified in Definitions~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} and~\\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} below.\n\\end{definition}\n\n\\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the classical low individual degree game]\\label{def:ld-question-distribution}\n\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, lem:cl-concat, def:cl-canonical, def:line-representative}\n\tLet $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ be as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}. Define $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$ to be the $1$-level CL function on $V$ that projects onto $V_X$: for every $(u,s,v) \\in V$,\n\t\\begin{equation}\n\t\t\\label{eq:cl-ptf}\n\t\tL_{\\mathsf{Point}}(u,s,v) = (u,0,0)\\;.\n\t\\end{equation}\n\tFor $s \\in \\F_q$, let $\\chi(s)$ be the unique integer such that\n\t\\begin{equation}\n\t\t\\label{eq:chi-func}\n\t\ts = (\\chi(s)-1)\\,\\frac{q}{m} + r\n\t\\end{equation}\n\tfor some $0 \\le r < q/m$, where $s$ is interpreted as an integer in $\\{0,1,\\ldots,q-1\\}$ under the identification of $\\F_q$ with binary strings fixed in Chapter~\\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}. Since $m$ divides $q$, when $s$ is uniformly distributed on $\\F_q$ the index $\\chi(s)$ is uniformly distributed on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$. Define $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ by\n\t\\begin{equation}\n\t\t\\label{eq:cl-alnf}\n\t\tL_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v) = \\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\\, s,\\, 0\\bigr)\\quad\\text{for all } (u,s,v) \\in V\\;,\n\t\\end{equation}\n\twhere $i = \\chi(s)$ and $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ denotes the canonical linear map with one-dimensional kernel spanned by $v$, used to compute canonical representatives of lines (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}). The function $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the concatenation (in the sense of Lemma~\\ref{lem:cl-concat}) of the $1$-level CL function projecting $V_I \\oplus V_V$ onto $V_I$ with the family of $1$-level CL functions $\\{L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}\\}$ on $V_X$ indexed by $i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$; thus $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is a $2$-level CL function. Define $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ by\n\t\\begin{equation}\n\t\t\\label{eq:cl-dlnf}\n\t\tL_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v) = \\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{\\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\\, s,\\, \\pi_{i-1}(v)\\bigr)\\;,\n\t\\end{equation}\n\twhere $i = \\chi(s)$ and $\\pi_{i-1}$ zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input. The function $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the concatenation of (i) the identity on $V_I$, (ii) for each $i$ the $1$-level CL function $v \\mapsto \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ on $V_V$, and (iii) for each pair $(s,v') \\in V_I \\oplus V_V$ the $1$-level CL function $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ on $V_X$; thus $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is a $3$-level CL function.\n\n\tThe question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is the typed CL distribution obtained as follows: sample a type pair $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ uniformly from $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, sample $z = (u,s,v)$ uniformly from $V$, and send each player $w \\in \\{\\mathrm A,\\mathrm B\\}$ the question $(t_w, L_{t_w}(z))$.\n\\end{definition}\n\nThe next two lemmas show that the CL functions $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ give rise to the axis-parallel and diagonal line-versus-point distributions.\nWe label the coordinates by $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,m-1\\}$, with label $r$\nrepresenting the paper's coordinate $r+1$.\n\n\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:alnf}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_mem_line}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, e_i)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a line that goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\n\t\\uses{def:line-representative}\n\tSince $s$ is uniformly random in $\\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$, the index $i = \\chi(s)$ is uniformly random in $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$, so $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$. Since $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u)$ is the canonical representative of the line through $u$ in direction $e_i$, we have $u \\in \\ell(u_0,e_i)$.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:dlnf}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_mem_line, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_prefix_zero}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, v)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a random diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares its first $i-1$ coordinates with $u$, for uniformly random $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\n\t\\uses{lem:alnf}\n\tThe proof is identical to that of Lemma~\\ref{lem:alnf}: uniformity of $s$ makes $i = \\chi(s)$ uniform, the direction component of the sampled tuple is $\\pi_{i-1}(v)$ for uniform $v$ (so its first $i-1$ coordinates vanish), and $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{\\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u)$ places $u$ on the line $\\ell(u_0,\\pi_{i-1}(v))$.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]\\label{def:line-point-dist}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineKind, MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineDesc}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_isProbability}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_isProbability}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_isProbability}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, lem:alnf, lem:dlnf}\n\tThe \\emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,e_i),\\, u)$, where we omit the $0$ components for simplicity. The \\emph{diagonal line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,s,v),\\, u)$. The \\emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{Line}}$ is the equal mixture of the two: with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, and with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$.\n\\end{definition}\n\n\\begin{definition}[Win predicate of the classical low individual degree game]\\label{def:ld-win-predicate}\n\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line, def:polyfunc}\n\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$. Answers in the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ take the following forms, depending on the question type; answers not of the prescribed form are rejected.\n\t\\begin{itemize}\n\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{Point}$, question content $u \\in \\F_q^m$: the answer is an element of $\\F_q^k$.\n\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{ALine}$, question content $(u_0,s) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q$, specifying the axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$ with $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple $(f_1,\\ldots,f_k)$ of univariate polynomials $f_j\\colon \\F_q \\to \\F_q$ of degree at most $d$, each given by its $d+1$ coefficients.\n\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{DLine}$, question content $(u_0,s,v) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q \\times \\F_q^m$, specifying the diagonal line $\\ell(u_0,v')$ with $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple of univariate polynomials of degree at most $md$.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_29","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc 'cat docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex'","aggregated_output":"\\documentclass[11pt]{article}\n\n\\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}\n\\usepackage{xurl}\n\\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}\n\\setlength{\\emergencystretch}{2em}\n\n\\input{command}\n\n\\title{Dimension Divisibility in the Classical Test Instantiation of the\n\tPauli Basis Analysis}\n\\author{}\n\\date{2026-08-30}\n\n\\begin{document}\n\\maketitle\n\n\\section{At a glance}\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\textbf{Difficulty: medium.}  Two related matters are recorded.\n  First, the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test invokes the\n  classical low individual degree game at dimension $2m+2$, and the game's\n  question distribution is undefined at that dimension for the admissible\n  parameters: it requires $2m+2$ to divide $q$, while admissibility supplies\n  only $m \\mid q$; the repair is a statement-level reformulation of an\n  imported theorem, not a new proof.  Second, the import of the classical\n  game's quantum soundness from the tensor-code paper carries two open\n  verification obligations at every dimension: the asserted identity with\n  the cited tensor-code test is not an identity and must be replaced by a\n  reduction with a value bound, and the source's instantiation of the\n  theorem's auxiliary parameter violates its lower bound at small\n  dimensions (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}).\n  \\item \\textbf{Estimated weight:} for the recommended direction, about\n  \\textbf{3--5 new definitions or interfaces} (a line-point distribution with\n  directly sampled index at arbitrary dimension, the directly indexed game,\n  and a restated soundness import) plus \\textbf{7--10 supporting lemmas},\n  including the strategy-transport layer between the directly indexed game\n  and the $\\chi$-based game (parsing pullback, seed-fiber averaging with\n  its open synchronicity-branch control, and a dilation--compression round\n  trip of the soundness conclusion); several hundred lines of formal proof.\n  Discharging the import obligations of\n  Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations} adds the pair-measurement\n  construction with its distributional matching, the branch-weight value\n  bound, and the parameter-bound case split.  The padding fallback is\n  heavier, roughly 6--10 reworked lemmas.\n  \\item \\textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \\textbf{15\\% Mathlib}\n  and \\textbf{85\\% project-local}.  Mathlib supplies uniform distributions on\n  finite types and pushforward identities; the substance is choosing the\n  statement of the imported soundness theorem and rechecking the combining\n  subtree against it.\n  \\item \\textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} uniform distributions on finite types\n  and their maps, and elementary divisibility arithmetic on powers of two.\n  The main inputs are project-local: the classical game, its conditionally\n  linear question distribution, and the imported soundness statement.\n  Tracked in \\localissue{0002}.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\section{Key theorem forms}\n\nThroughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple\n$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \\ge 1$ and $m \\mid q$, and\n$\\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives\nover $\\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four\ntheorem forms.\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item \\textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There\n  is a function $\\delta_S(\\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,\n  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every\n  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test\n  succeeding with probability at least $1-\\eps$, there is a projective\n  measurement $\\{\\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in\n  $\\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\\delta_S$-consistent, on\n  average over a uniform point $u \\in \\F_q^m$ and in both bases\n  $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, with the corresponding points measurements\n  $\\{\\hat M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\\}$ of the strategy, together with the\n  symmetric counterpart of this relation.\n  \\item \\textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low\n  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\\, 2m+2,\\, d,\\, 1)$ is well\n  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the\n  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least\n  $1 - \\delta_{\\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws\n  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function\n  $\\chi_{2m+2}\\colon \\F_q \\to \\{1,\\ldots,2m+2\\}$ with classes of equal size\n  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.\n  \\item \\textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source\n  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \\mid q$.  Among\n  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and\n  $q \\ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$ and for\n  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.\n  \\item \\textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum\n  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual\n  degree game over $\\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \\ge 1$ and\n  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question\n  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,\n  uniformly from $\\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$ directly rather than through an index\n  function on $\\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in\n  place of the seed $s \\in \\F_q$; the error is\n  $\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}(\\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\\eps^b + q^{-b} +\n  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:\n  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\\chi$-based\n  import (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present\n  form from it when $m' \\mid q$ requires the strategy transport described\n  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open\n  obligation.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}\n\nWe examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical\nlow-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression\npaper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,\narXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low\nindividual degree test of \\cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%\n\\footnote{Tracked in \\localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source\nconsulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at\n\\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},\nlines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined\nline lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization\nwith its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its\nproof, and admissibility are at\n\\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},\nlines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}\nThere, the combined point measurements\n$\\{\\hat Q^{x,z,\\alpha,\\beta}_c\\}$ and combined line measurements\n$\\{\\hat Q^{\\ell}_f\\}$, indexed by points of $\\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in\n$\\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low\nindividual degree game with parameters\n\\[\n  \\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\\, 2m+2,\\, d,\\, 1)\n  \\tag{\\path{lem:qld-4-7}}\n\\]\nof value $1 - \\delta_{\\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem\nfor that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.\nThe two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution\nover $\\F_q^{2m+2}$.\n\nThe game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an\nadmissible field size \\emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not\nincidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution\nin which a uniform seed coordinate $s \\in \\F_q$, read as an integer in\n$\\{0,\\ldots,q-1\\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique\n$\\chi(s)$ with\n\\[\n  s = (\\chi(s)-1)\\,\\frac{q}{m'} + r, \\qquad 0 \\le r < \\frac{q}{m'},\n  \\tag{\\path{eq:chi-func}}\n\\]\nso that the $m'$ classes $\\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\\F_q$ into sets of equal\nsize $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \\nmid q$ neither the index\nfunction nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.\n\nAdmissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \\mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$\nis a power of two, $m \\mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \\ge 1$ the integer\n$m+1 \\ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and\ndivides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \\mid q$ holds for every\nadmissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is\nundefined for every admissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$: for instance\n$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \\nmid 8$.  The source performs\nthe instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route\nestablishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for\nthe Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \\ge 8$.\n\n\\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}\n\\label{sec:import-obligations}\n\nThe quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint\n$m' \\mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its\nproof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \\mid q$, asserts that the game with\nsimultaneity parameter $1$ is \\emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code\ntest for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\\mathcal C^{\\ot m'}$ of the same\nauthors' \\emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)\n\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with\nthat theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,\nand written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the\nsimultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither\nthe asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the\nimport carries two verification obligations, which this section details and\nwhich the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as\nopen.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they\narise at every dimension, for the $\\chi$-based game where it is defined and\nequally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate\nrepairs.\n\n\\paragraph{The cited test.}\nIn the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of\n\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness\nmeasure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of\nthree subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each\nsubtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \\emph{Axis-parallel lines\ntest}: sample a uniform point $u \\in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis\n$j \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\\ell$ through $u$ in\ndirection $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \\in \\mathcal C$;\nsend $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff\n$g(u_j) = a$.  \\emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample\n$j \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$ and a subcube $H \\subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the\nlast $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly\nin $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to\none prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to\nthe other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \\emph{Synchronicity\ntest}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered\npair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their\nanswers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this\ntest with probability $1-\\eps$ together with an integer parameter\n$K \\ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code\n--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and\ndistance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements\n$\\{G_c\\}$ and $\\{\\tilde G_c\\}$ with outcomes in $\\mathcal C^{\\ot m'}$,\nconsistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's\nlines measurements, and with each other, up to\n$\\eta'(m',t,K,\\eps,n^{-1}) = \\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \\cdot\n\\mathrm{poly}(\\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}\nThe source asserts that the $\\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$\nis this test.  It is not, in four respects.\n(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals\ntwo points of a \\emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent\n--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line\nquestion reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$\npolynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the\ndiagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$\nand $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and\nboth directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line\ndescription carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of\nthe pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the\ncompatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the\n\\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the\n\\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The\nconstruction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the\nhidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.\n(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \\in \\F_q$; the test's\ncarry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class\n$\\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging\ndifficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves\nthe line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.\n(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$\nin the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are\nmatched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's\nrejection probability in the test is at most $\\tfrac32$ times the game's\nrejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is\nthe target of the obligation, not an established fact.\n(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal\nquestions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most\n$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for\nwhich the test has no counterpart branch.\nFinally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points\nmeasurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the\nfirst prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines\nmeasurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency\nin both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization\nof the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is\ndifficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together\nthey replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its\nown value bound.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}\nTheorem~4.7 requires $K \\ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source\ninstantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff\n$(m')^2 d \\ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \\ge 1$ when $m' \\ge 5$,\nholds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \\ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when\n$m' \\le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the\nadmissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's\ninstantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \\in \\{1,2\\}$ for\nevery $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \\in \\{1,2\\}$ --- in particular, in the\nmultilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \\le 4$. The low\nindividual degree test of \\cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} samples its axis\nindex $i$ uniformly from $\\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$ directly, with no index function\non $\\F_q$ and no divisibility hypothesis,%\n\\footnote{See the test figure in \\path{references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex}.}\nand the tensor-code test is likewise a test about the code\n$\\mathcal C^{\\ot m'}$, not about an encoding of indices into $\\F_q$.  The\n$\\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is\nconditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the\ngame the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,\nwhere admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension\n$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the\nproof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question\ndistribution to be conditionally linear.\n\n\\section{Candidate repairs}\n\n\\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}\nDefine, for arbitrary $m' \\ge 1$, the line-point distribution over\n$\\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index\n$i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first\n$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \\emph{directly indexed game} with\nthis question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,\nfor diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed\n$s \\in \\F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game\n(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing\nelse: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed\nlines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game\ndoes, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as\nthe $\\chi$-based import (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at\narbitrary dimension.\n\nThe relation to the present game when $m' \\mid q$ must moreover be proved\nat the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the\ntwo games have different question alphabets: an $\\mathsf{ALine}$ question\nof the $\\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\\mathsf{DLine}$\nquestion a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different\nmeasurements for seeds $s \\ne s'$ with $\\chi(s) = \\chi(s')$, and equality\nof the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport\nsuch a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following\nobligations, none of which is carried out here.\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \\mid q$, the image of the\n  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map\n  $(u_0,s) \\mapsto (u_0,\\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \\mapsto (u_0,\\chi(s),v')$\n  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the\n  seed is uniform on the class $\\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything\n  else.\n  \\item \\emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game\n  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the\n  $\\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only\n  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers\n  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity\n  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be\n  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This\n  is the direction the combining subtree needs.\n  \\item \\emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does\n  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its\n  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively\n  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \\in \\chi^{-1}(i)$ of the\n  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving\n  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the\n  seed this preserves the value of every \\emph{line-versus-point} branch\n  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value\n  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged\n  measurement computes.  It does \\emph{not} preserve the synchronicity\n  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\\chi$-based\n  branch value is the diagonal average\n  $\\E_{s}\\sum_f \\langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \\ot \\widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f\n  \\rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average\n  $\\E_{s,s'}\\sum_f \\langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \\ot \\widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f\n  \\rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever\n  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if\n  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is\n  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the\n  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the\n  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that\n  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the\n  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show\n  that a strategy of value $1-\\eps$ in the $\\chi$-based game is, with\n  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a\n  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on\n  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open\n  obligation.\n  \\item \\emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM\n  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported\n  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The\n  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one\n  (Naimark preserves all product correlations\n  $\\langle X \\ot Y \\rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated\n  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---\n  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging\n  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial\n  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required\n  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression\n  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is\n  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4\n  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside\n  the import.)\n\\end{itemize}\n\nThe combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution\nand the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes\nwell defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the\nproofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are\nindexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them\n--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,\nwith no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use\nonly the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity\nof the sampling is part of this direction's obligations. In the complementary regime $m \\in \\{q/2,\\, q\\}$ the\nconclusion is vacuous: $md \\ge q/2$ gives\n$\\delta_S \\ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \\ge a\\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \\ge a\\,2^{-b} \\ge 1$\nfor $a \\ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never\nexceed $1$. Their proofs retain the source\nconstructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the\nfirst sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\\chi_{2m+2}$ and\nthe line-point distribution over $\\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the\ninstantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is\nused as a game parameter tuple. An earlier revision had\ninstead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \\mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was\nstatement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis\nexcludes all admissible $m \\ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nThere is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low\nindividual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every\nadmissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its\nquestion distribution requires $2m+2 \\mid q$ while admissibility supplies\nonly $m \\mid q$. {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_33","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '333,438p' docs/formalization-patterns.md\"","aggregated_output":"## Pattern 3: Split-module architecture\n\n### Directory structure\n\nThe Lean codebase is organized into per-chapter subdirectories under\n`MIPStarRE/LDT/`, each with its own internal structure:\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/LDT/\n├── Basic/                    # Parameters, operators, submeasurements, distributions\n├── Test/                     # Test definitions, main theorem, error cascade\n├── Preliminaries/            # Polynomials, finite fields, Cauchy–Schwarz, Fourier\n├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/   # Orthonormalization, projective completion\n├── MainInductionStep/        # Section 6 induction theorem\n├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/  # Section 7–8 expansion, global variance\n├── GlobalVariance/           # Section 8.5 (and related global variance machinery)\n├── SelfImprovement/          # Section 9 self-improvement\n├── CommutativityPoints/      # Section 10 commutativity setup\n├── Tactic/                   # Section 10 proof orchestration utilities\n├── Commutativity/            # Section 11 commutativity bounds\n└── Pasting/                  # Section 12 pasting\n```\n\n### Subdirectory layout convention\n\nEach subdirectory follows a consistent internal layout:\n\n```\nSubModule/\n├── Defs.lean        # New structures, type abbreviations, error-term definitions\n├── Statements.lean   # Statement-level types (hypothesis bundles, conclusion shapes)\n├── Theorems.lean     # Public re-export, when the section has one\n└── Theorems/\n    ├── Core.lean     # Main proof of the chapter's theorem\n    ├── ...           # Supporting proof leaves\n    └── Results.lean  # Re-export file for the proof leaves\n```\n\nSome larger chapters (like `Pasting/` and `SelfImprovement/`) have more\ninternal subdivisions (e.g., `Pasting/Bernoulli/`, `Pasting/Sandwich/`,\n`SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/`).  When an outer `Theorems.lean` module is\npresent, it imports the public proof leaves.\n\n### Why split instead of monolithic files?\n\n| Reason | Details |\n|--------|---------|\n| **Compilation parallelism** | Lean's per-file compilation is single-threaded per file; smaller files mean faster individual type-checking loops |\n| **Dependency isolation** | A proof leaf in `Pasting/Sandwich/` only depends on `Pasting/Defs.lean` and `Pasting/Statements.lean`, not on the entire pasting proof chain |\n| **Edit locality** | Changing a helper in `SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/AddInUStep12/Raw.lean` does not re-elaborate unrelated downstream leaves unless the helper's type changed |\n| **Reviewability** | A 200-line proof leaf is easier to review than a 4000-line monolithic proof block |\n| **Parallel agent work** | Different agents can work on different proof leaves concurrently without merge conflicts |\n\n### When *not* to split further\n\nDon't split a file just to have one theorem per file.  A single file\ncontaining 3–5 related lemmas that share helper definitions and proof\nstructure is better than 5 files each with one lemma and duplicate\nhelper material.\n\nWhen splitting does happen, the new leaves, declarations, and module\nnames must follow the mathematical naming norm in\n`docs/mathematical_language.md`: name the mathematical boundary, not\nthe paper line number, workflow step, or implementation phase.\n\n### Re-export files\n\nSee [Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)\nbelow.\n\n---\n\n## Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern\n\nPublic subdirectories with several proof leaves may have a root-level\nre-export file that imports the source-facing leaves.  For example, the\ntop-level LDT module imports the public section APIs:\n\n```lean\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.ProjectivizationChain.Output\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.MainInductionStep.Theorems.MainTheorems.Successor\nimport MIPStarRE.LDT.Pasting.Bernoulli.Final\n```\n\nThe re-export module itself contains no new mathematical declarations. It is a\npublic import convenience.  When no such public module exists, downstream code\nshould import the specific leaf module whose declarations it uses.\n\nThe top-level re-export file is `MIPStarRE.lean`, which imports all\nsubdirectories.  `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean` imports all LDT subdirectories.\n\n**When to add to a re-export file**: When a new proof leaf is added to a\npublic theorem or definition subdirectory and the leaf is part of the intended\nsection-level API, add its import to the relevant public module.\n\n**When not to add**: If a leaf is only used by one other leaf (internal\nhelper), do not add it to a public re-export module; let the consumer import it\ndirectly so its API surface does not leak.\n\n**When not to create another wrapper**: Do not add an intermediate module whose\nonly purpose is to import a single leaf, or a wrapper that is itself imported\nonly by a public re-export module.  The public module should import the\nconcrete leaf directly.  Such one-step wrappers make the import graph harder to\nread without recording any new mathematical boundary.\n\n---\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class\n$\\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging\ndifficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves\nthe line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.\n(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$\nin the test against $2/9$ in the game. In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the\nadmissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's\ninstantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \\in \\{1,2\\}$ for\nevery $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \\in \\{1,2\\}$ --- in particular, in the\nmultilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \\le 4$. The underlying\nmathematics does not need the divisibility. The\n$\\chi$-based packaging exists so that the question distribution is\nconditionally linear, which the introspection machinery requires for the\ngame the players actually play --- the Pauli basis test at dimension $m$,\nwhere admissibility does supply the divisibility.  The game at dimension\n$2m+2$ never appears in a verifier; it is an internal analysis device in the\nproof of the polynomial-pair lemma, so nothing there requires its question\ndistribution to be conditionally linear.\n\n\\section{Candidate repairs}\n\n\\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}\nDefine, for arbitrary $m' \\ge 1$, the line-point distribution over\n$\\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index\n$i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first\n$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \\emph{directly indexed game} with\nthis question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,\nfor diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed\n$s \\in \\F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game\n(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing\nelse: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed\nlines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game\ndoes, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as\nthe $\\chi$-based import (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at\narbitrary dimension.\n\nThe relation to the present game when $m' \\mid q$ must moreover be proved\nat the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the\ntwo games have different question alphabets: an $\\mathsf{ALine}$ question\nof the $\\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\\mathsf{DLine}$\nquestion a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different\nmeasurements for seeds $s \\ne s'$ with $\\chi(s) = \\chi(s')$, and equality\nof the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport\nsuch a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following\nobligations, none of which is carried out here.\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \\mid q$, the image of the\n  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map\n  $(u_0,s) \\mapsto (u_0,\\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \\mapsto (u_0,\\chi(s),v')$\n  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the\n  seed is uniform on the class $\\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything\n  else.\n  \\item \\emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game\n  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the\n  $\\chi$-based game. {"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_37","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '360,560p' docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex\"","aggregated_output":"  \\item \\emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM\n  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported\n  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The\n  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one\n  (Naimark preserves all product correlations\n  $\\langle X \\ot Y \\rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated\n  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---\n  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging\n  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial\n  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required\n  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression\n  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is\n  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4\n  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside\n  the import.)\n\\end{itemize}\n\nThe combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution\nand the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes\nwell defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the\nproofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are\nindexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them\n--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,\nwith no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use\nonly the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity\nof the sampling is part of this direction's obligations.  This follows the\nsubtree protocol for a definition-level mismatch: the definition is\ncorrected at the lowest point rather than each downstream lemma acquiring\na hypothesis.  The transport layer costs one parsing-map definition, the\ndistribution lemma, the pullback lemma, whichever synchronicity control is\nchosen, and the dilation--compression lemma; the first three are an\nestimated one to two hundred lines on top of the restated import, with the\nblueprint's existing Naimark interface supplying the dilation, while the\nsynchronicity control is the step whose weight is genuinely uncertain.\nThe external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples\nits axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1\nthere draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,\nwith no index encoding into $\\F_q$.\n\n\\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}\nAlternatively, embed the combined polynomial into\n$\\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\\bar m}(\\F_q)$ for $\\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two\nwith $\\bar m \\ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then\n$\\bar m \\mid q$ holds whenever $q \\ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at\ndimension $\\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \\in \\{q/2,\\, q\\}$ the\nconclusion is vacuous: $md \\ge q/2$ gives\n$\\delta_S \\ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \\ge a\\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \\ge a\\,2^{-b} \\ge 1$\nfor $a \\ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never\nexceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the\nsub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining\nmap, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the\ncombining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.\n\n\\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}\nOne could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes\nof sizes $\\lfloor q/(2m+2)\\rfloor$ and $\\lceil q/(2m+2)\\rceil$.  The index\nis then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external\ntest fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line\nanalysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported\nsoundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.\n\n\\section{Comparison with the blueprint}\n\nThe blueprint \\cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the\ncombined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped\nstatements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source\nconstructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the\nfirst sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\\chi_{2m+2}$ and\nthe line-point distribution over $\\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the\ninstantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is\nused as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility\narithmetic and cites this note; the final soundness theorem for the Pauli\nbasis test remains open modulo this obligation.  The blueprint's proof node\nfor the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the\nidentification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of\nTheorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of\nSection~\\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the\ndetailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  An earlier revision had\ninstead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \\mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was\nstatement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis\nexcludes all admissible $m \\ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nThere is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low\nindividual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every\nadmissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its\nquestion distribution requires $2m+2 \\mid q$ while admissibility supplies\nonly $m \\mid q$.  The cited route therefore does not establish the\npolynomial-pair lemma, nor the soundness of the Pauli basis test that\ndepends on it, beyond $m = 1$ and $q \\ge 8$.  Independently of the\ndivisibility, the import of the classical game's quantum soundness carries\nthe two open verification obligations of\nSection~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}: the asserted identity with the\ntwo-prover tensor-code test must be replaced by a reduction carrying a\nvalue bound, and the source's instantiation of the auxiliary parameter\nviolates the theorem's lower bound at the small dimensions listed there.\nWe do not assert that any conclusion is false: the underlying tensor-code\nsoundness is insensitive to how the axis index is sampled, and both import\nobligations concern verification, not counterexample. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Nothing is run in the primary\ncheckout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the\nrun starts.\n\nExit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at\nleast one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start\n(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —\na GitHub error never degrades to a local record).\n\n### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips\n\n| Precondition | Why it is fatal |\n|---|---|\n| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |\n| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |\n| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the \"checks silently stopped running\" failure the parent repo patched twice |\n| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |\n| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |\n\nThere is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`\nand `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely\nstops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green\nlight it never earned. Job table\n\nEight steps, in this order, named exactly after the parent workflow's job ids\nso the auto-fix dispatcher's mapping (build → ci-fix, blueprint-render →\nblueprint-fix, everything else → never auto-fixed) ports without translation.\n\n| Step | Parent job | What it runs (in the worktree) | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `build` | `build` (`pr-ci.yml:115-168`) | warm `.lake/build`, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build`, `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit` (`:155-156`), `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` (`:158-159`) | `lean ∨ comparator ∨ workflow` |\n| --base-ref` | `lean ∨ blueprint ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |\n| `file-length` | `file-length` (`:319-340`) | `check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .` (>1000 lines) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |\n| Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run\n```\n\nA run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;\n`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`.
